transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to. It’s like I’ve got a little motor running under my skin. In staff meetings, or even briefings for church events, I’m shifting around, standing up, or looking for some reason to go do something. It’s getting hard to ignore.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or intensely energized for days at a time?
No, I don’t think so. I get restless and wound up, but not like happy or “on top of the world” for days or anything like that.
When you were a child, were you also the kind of person who had trouble sitting still?

Yes. I remember in grade school getting in trouble for jumping out of my seat, talking over the teacher, and starting things before she even finished giving directions. My mother used to say I was wound too tight, even back then.
Do you often have trouble sustaining attention on tasks, like losing focus during reading, conversations, or paperwork?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of it so much as losing focus on reading or paperwork. I mean, I can usually follow along if I need to. The bigger thing I notice is more that I get physically antsy, but as far as attention itself, I haven’t paid a lot of attention to that.
Do you often find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?
I don’t really know. I mean, I worry about normal stuff like bills or work things, but I wouldn’t say it’s excessive. It’s not something I’ve really noticed as a big problem.
Do you often act or speak before thinking?

Yes, I do. Like when my supervisor or someone at the church is giving me instructions, I’ll jump in before they’re done because I think I know what they’re about to say. Sometimes I’m wrong, and then they have to stop and correct me.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your mind drifts or you get distracted?

I’m not really sure about that one. I don’t notice my mind drifting so much that I can’t finish things. If I don’t finish something, I’d have to think about why, but I wouldn’t say distraction is the main thing I’ve noticed.
Do you often misplace things you need, like keys, paperwork, or your phone?
Not really that I can think of. I mean, I’ll set something down now and then like anybody, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular problem with my keys or phone or paperwork.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed organization being a big problem for me. I usually just do what needs doing, especially at work. I’d have to think about it more, but nothing really stands out.
Do you often avoid or put off tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like paperwork, reading, or detailed forms?

I don’t think so, not in any clear way. I mean, paperwork and forms aren’t my favorite, but I wouldn’t say I regularly avoid them or put them off because of the mental effort. Nothing like that really stands out to me.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss details?
I don’t think that’s a big issue for me. I mean, I can make a mistake here and there like anyone, but I haven’t noticed a pattern of missing details or making careless mistakes often.
Do you often get distracted by things going on around you?
Not especially, no. I mean, if there’s a loud noise or someone walks in, I’ll notice it, but I don’t feel like I’m constantly getting pulled away by stuff around me. Nothing major that I’ve noticed.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn?

Yeah, I do. Waiting on other people at work gets to me — like waiting for the freight elevator, or for the supply closet key, or for someone to tell me which room needs cleaning next. I get antsy and short, and I’ll pace around or try to push things along before it’s really my turn.
Do you often interrupt other people when they’re talking?

Yes, I do that. Like when my supervisor or someone from the church staff is giving me instructions, I’ll jump in before they finish because I think I know what they’re about to say. Sometimes I’m wrong, and then they have to stop and correct me.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions and end up leaving tasks unfinished?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I leave things unfinished that much, at least not that I’ve noticed. If I’m given clear instructions, I usually try to get it done. I might need something repeated now and then, but I wouldn’t say that’s a big problem for me.
Do you often have difficulty paying close attention when doing work that requires focus?

I’m not really sure on that one. I mean, I can usually do my cleaning work if I know what needs doing. I haven’t noticed a big problem with paying attention, unless I’m tired or there’s a lot going on around me. But I wouldn’t say it happens all the time.
Do you often have trouble listening when someone is speaking directly to you?
I’m not sure. I mean, I try to listen when someone’s talking right to me. Sometimes I might miss a piece of what they said, but I haven’t really noticed it being a big problem.
Do you often fail to finish tasks because you get distracted?

I don’t really think so. I mean, I might get sidetracked once in a while like anyone, but I haven’t noticed that I’m often failing to finish things because of it. If I start a job, I usually try to get it done.
Do you often fidget with your hands or feet, or squirm in your seat?

Yes, that one fits. When I’m supposed to sit still, like in a staff meeting or a church briefing, I feel like there’s a motor running under my skin. I’ll shift around, move my hands or feet, or end up standing up if I can. Sometimes I’ll look for an excuse to go do something just so I can move.
As an adult, do you often feel restless, like you’re driven to keep moving even when it would be better to stay still?

Yes, I do. That’s actually a big part of why I came in. When I’m supposed to sit still, like in staff meetings or church event briefings, I feel like I’ve got a motor humming under my skin. I start shifting around, or I’ll stand up if I can, or find some excuse to move around.
